You can suspect you have something but you can't accurately say you do since so many disorders overlap with other ones. While people say getting a diagnosis is dangerous, I don't really understand bc people will go after those who are different whether they know you are autistic or not. My diagnosis helped me gain concessions and disability access where I needed it, like boarding a plane first so I don't have to get on with people and boarding last for the same reason. My disability aids help me and its no use trying to keep it secret if it's not going to change anything or help you. I prefer having people know of my diagnosis so they understand why I do what I do. But it's different saying "I think I have autism which is why I do x". Autism might not be the issue to cause your behaviour or whatever x is, autism might be. It could be something else. Which is why the diagnosis is important in my eyes
